# sdidlab

Synthetic difference-in-differences for a single treated unit, with the
inference and diagnostics that design needs.

`sdidlab` is built around the
[synthdid](https://github.com/synth-inference/synthdid) estimator of
Arkhangelsky, Athey, Hirshberg, Imbens and Wager (2021). Where it
reproduces synthdid, it does so exactly: point estimates, unit and time
weights, and placebo standard errors match synthdid to machine
precision, and the test suite enforces it. On top of that it adds:

- **Trimmed placebo inference.** In a large, heterogeneous donor pool,
  many placebo draws are fitted badly and inflate the placebo standard
  error.
  [`placebo_se_trimmed()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/placebo_se_trimmed.md)
  drops placebos whose pre-period fit is more than `trim_k` times worse
  than the treated unit’s. It trims the *inference* distribution, never
  the donor pool.
- **Fit diagnostics that respect SDID.** SDID absorbs a constant level
  gap between the treated unit and its synthetic control, so
  `trend_rmse` measures the pre-period gap *after* removing its mean, on
  the covariate-adjusted outcome when covariates are used.
- **Two covariate routes.** Hand covariates to synthdid, or residualise
  the outcome on untreated cells first (Kranz 2022) with
  [`project_out_covariates()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/project_out_covariates.md).
- **A bias-corrected synthetic control.**
  [`fit_scm()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/fit_scm.md)
  implements the Abadie–Diamond–Hainmueller estimator with predictor
  matching, the Abadie–L’Hour bias correction, an optional Abadie–L’Hour
  penalty that makes the weights unique, and ranked-RMSPE permutation
  inference through
  [`scm_placebo_permutation()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/scm_placebo_permutation.md)
  and
  [`rmspe_pvalue()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/rmspe_pvalue.md).
  The weights are solved exactly by an active-set method, and an exact
  pre-period fit – where the weights, and therefore the estimate, are
  not unique – is flagged rather than silently resolved.

## Installation

synthdid is not on CRAN, so install both from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("James-Hodges/sdidlab")
```

The `Remotes` field pins synthdid to the commit the parity tests were
run against.

## Example: California’s Proposition 99

``` r

library(sdidlab)

data("california_prop99", package = "synthdid")
setup <- synthdid::panel.matrices(california_prop99)

set.seed(1)
fit <- fit_sdid(setup$Y, setup$N0, setup$T0, replications = 200, trim_k = 5)

fit$att                 # -15.6 packs per capita, as in Arkhangelsky et al.
c(fit$ci_lo, fit$ci_hi) # placebo-based 95% interval
fit$trend_rmse          # pre-period fit, level gap removed
fit$placebos_kept       # how many of the 200 placebos survived trimming
```

With `trim_k = Inf` the standard error is synthdid’s own placebo
standard error, draw for draw under the same seed.

The synthetic-control alternative:

``` r

scm <- fit_scm(setup$Y, setup$N0, setup$T0, v_method = "mspe")
scm$att                 # bias-corrected ATT

perm <- scm_placebo_permutation(setup$Y, setup$N0, setup$T0, v_method = "mspe")
r <- perm$results
rmspe_pvalue(setNames(r$rmspe_ratio_raw, r$unit), r$att, r$unit[r$treated])
```

## Workflow

For more than a one-off fit, describe each model as a **specification**
and let sdidlab handle the bookkeeping:

``` r

panel <- prop99_panel()          # or sdid_panel(your_data, unit = , time = , outcome = )
spec  <- sdid_spec(label = "Prop 99", inference = list(replications = 200))
run   <- fit_spec(spec, panel, seed = seed_for(spec), store = "runs")

plot_sdid_trajectory(run)
plot_gap_path(run)
plot_placebo_distribution(run)
```

Specifications hash to a stable identifier, round-trip through YAML (one
file can hold a whole robustness sweep), and fitted runs are saved so
they can be reloaded and re-plotted without refitting.
[`write_spec_script()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/write_spec_script.md)
writes a self-contained R script that reproduces every fit exactly.

[`run_demo()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/run_demo.md)
opens an interactive app that does all of this in the browser: build a
specification, fit it, inspect every diagnostic, compare fits, and
download the specifications and a reproducing script.

The articles cover each part in depth:

- [Getting
  started](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/articles/sdidlab.html)
- [Specifications, sweeps and the run
  store](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/articles/specs-and-runs.html)
- [Placebo inference with one treated
  unit](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/articles/placebo-inference.html)
- [Synthetic control: bias correction, exact fits and permutation
  inference](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/articles/synthetic-control.html)

## Validation

The test suite checks sdidlab against independent implementations, not
just against itself:

| What | Checked against |
|----|----|
| SDID, SC and DiD estimates and weights | `synthdid`, to 1e-12 |
| Placebo standard errors (untrimmed), with and without covariates | `synthdid::vcov(method = "placebo")`, to 1e-10 under the same seed |
| Covariate residualisation | Two-way fixed-effects OLS on untreated cells, and `fixest` |
| Synthetic-control weights, plain and penalised | The KKT optimality conditions; an independent long-run solve; `Synth` with the same `V` |
| Bias correction | An independent per-period OLS computation |

## References

Abadie, A., Diamond, A. and Hainmueller, J. (2010). Synthetic Control
Methods for Comparative Case Studies. *Journal of the American
Statistical Association* 105(490), 493–505.

Abadie, A. and L’Hour, J. (2021). A Penalized Synthetic Control
Estimator for Disaggregated Data. *Journal of the American Statistical
Association* 116(536), 1817–1834.

Arkhangelsky, D., Athey, S., Hirshberg, D. A., Imbens, G. W. and Wager,
S. (2021). Synthetic Difference-in-Differences. *American Economic
Review* 111(12), 4088–4118.

Kranz, S. (2022). Synthetic Difference-in-Differences with Time-Varying
Covariates. Working paper.

  : Declare a long panel for sdidlab

  : California's Proposition 99 as an sdid_panel
- [`sdid_spec()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/sdid_spec.md)
  : Build a specification
- [`spec_hash()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/spec_hash.md)
  : A specification's stable identifier
- [`write_spec_yaml()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/spec_yaml.md)
  [`read_spec_yaml()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/spec_yaml.md)
  [`read_specs()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/spec_yaml.md)
  [`write_specs_yaml()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/spec_yaml.md)
  : Read and write specifications as YAML
- [`build_setup()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/build_setup.md)
  : Build the estimator inputs for a specification
- [`resolve_pool()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/resolve_pool.md)
  : Resolve a specification's donor pool
- [`register_outcome()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/registry.md)
  [`register_pool()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/registry.md)
  [`registered_outcomes()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/registry.md)
  [`registered_pools()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/registry.md)
  : Register derived outcomes and named donor pools

## Fitting

- [`fit_spec()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/fit_spec.md)
  : Fit one specification end to end
- [`run_specs()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/run_specs.md)
  : Fit a list of specifications
- [`seed_for()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/seed_for.md)
  : A specification's own seed
- [`save_run()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/run_store.md)
  [`load_run()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/run_store.md)
  [`refresh_runs_index()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/run_store.md)
  [`prune_runs()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/run_store.md)
  : Save, load and index fitted runs
- [`write_spec_script()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/write_spec_script.md)
  : Write a runnable R script for a set of specifications

## Estimators and inference

- [`fit_sdid()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/fit_sdid.md)
  : Fit one synthetic-DiD specification and return its full result set
- [`placebo_se_trimmed()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/placebo_se_trimmed.md)
  : Placebo standard error with poorly-fitting placebos trimmed
- [`adjusted_outcome()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/adjusted_outcome.md)
  : The outcome a synthdid estimate was actually fitted on
- [`project_out_covariates()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/project_out_covariates.md)
  : Residualise the outcome on covariates using untreated cells only
- [`fit_scm()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/fit_scm.md)
  : Fit a bias-corrected synthetic control
- [`sc_weights_simplex()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/sc_weights_simplex.md)
  : Simplex weights minimising a V-weighted predictor discrepancy
- [`scm_placebo_permutation()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/scm_placebo_permutation.md)
  : Permute treatment in space across every donor
- [`rmspe_pvalue()`](https://james-hodges.github.io/sdidlab/reference/rmspe_pvalue.md)
  : Ranked-RMSPE permutation p-value for a synthetic control
